ios.desc:
Remember dialing into BBSes at 2400 baud? The slow reveal of ANSI art filling your terminal, character by character, while the modem crackled in the background?

ANSI Saver turns your Apple TV into a gallery for that art. Thousands of ANSI and ASCII artpacks from the 80s, 90s, and today — displayed on the biggest screen in your house.

How it works

The app runs a small web server on your local network. Open the URL from your phone or laptop, and you can upload artpacks or browse the 16colo.rs archive — all without touching the remote. Your Apple TV does the rest.

Two ways to watch

Smooth mode scrolls through art with continuous flow and crossfades — the default, meant to be left running. Or switch to Modem mode: a faithful simulation of a dial-up connection, complete with character-by-character reveal, cursor blinking, and the occasional line noise glitch. Pick your baud rate from 300 to 56k.

Features

- Browse and download artpacks from 16colo.rs, the largest ANSI art archive
- Upload your own .zip artpacks from any device on your network
- Smooth and Modem display modes (300–56k baud simulation)
- Continuous scroll by default for an endless stream of art
- Now Playing overlay shows the pack and filename of whatever is on screen
- Preview files before downloading with server-side rendering
- Supports .ANS, .ICE, .ASC, and .TXT files
- CP437 font rendering with full 16-color CGA palette
- ICE color mode support
- Dark UI, no ads, no accounts, no tracking
- Runs entirely on your local network — your art stays on your device

Built for anyone who misses the art of the BBS era, or just discovered it.

quotes.text:
A while back I posted the macOS version here: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47288007

Now there's a tvOS version. The interesting part was getting artpacks onto an Apple TV without a keyboard, the app runs a small web server on your local network, so you upload packs or browse
16colo.rs from your phone and the TV plays from cache.

Paid this time; the macOS version stays free and open source.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ansi-saver/id6762137767
